notes: Background: mid-market product analytics SaaS. 300 engineers + product/CS. Heavy investment in conversational product assistant and in-app insight generation.
Current stack: vendor = OpenAI (chat/gpt-4 family) for user chat + embeddings for search. Monthly spend ~ $40k. Want lower unit cost and control over SLAs.
Primary goal: move from hosted API -> dedicated capacity once parity confirmed (hosted POC -> Dedicated pilot). Need same developer ergonomics and minimal prompt changes.
Traffic profile: peak 180 reqs/s (chat), 99th pct latency target < 200ms for short-turn prompts; embeddings workload asynchronous, ~1.5M vectors/month.
POC work: ported ~10k prompt templates to Redwood compat layer. Focus tests: customer support flows, billing queries, and insights extraction prompts.

Findings: observed prompt-parity regressions on ~6% of QA-type prompts. Regressions mainly around temperature/stop-token differences and system-prompt handling. SE working on tokenization/spacing normalization and model variant tuning.
Latency: Hosted API median ~45ms for local tests; 99th ~210ms — need kernel/config tweaks. SE suggested KV caching hot prefixes and shorter sequence kernels.
Routing/fallback: leadership insists on automatic fallback to current vendor for high-severity regressions until dedicated is green.
Security: procurement requires SSO (SAML) + audit logs + optional customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. Data residency: US only for now.
Regressions workflow requested: nightly regression suite (2k prompts) + signal to Redwood Optimize to suggest quantization/batch settings that preserve quality.
Quotes from CTTO: 'We need prompt parity or close to it — customer UX can't change overnight.'
Commercial: procurement asks for committed monthly throughput pricing for Dedicated + transitional hosted credits. Wants clear overage model and SLA on latency.
Next steps (short): run extended regression pass on 10k prompts with SE, produce side-by-side diff report; procurement to review pricing draft; schedule Dedicated pilot dates.
Risks: timeline tight (Q1 migration target), internal legal needs SOC2 report and KMS integration doc. If regressions persist, will do hybrid routing instead of full cutover.
